items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ حادثه «بین یک نفتکش و نیروهای نظامی» در دریای عمان

items.title: ادامه تلاش‌های میانجی‌های منطقه‌ای؛ نخست‌وزیر قطر با وزیر خارجه آمریکا در واشنگتن دیدار می‌کند
items.summary: مارکو روبیو، وزیر خارجه ایالات متحده، قرار است امروز در واشنگتن‌ با محمد بن عبدالرحمن بن جاسم آل ثانی، نخست‌وزیر و وزیر خارجه قطر، دیدار کند. روز جمعه هم برد کوپر، فرمانده سنتکام، با سعود بن عبدالرحمن آل ثانی، وزیر دفاع قطر در دوحه دیدار کرده بود و همزمان کاظم غریب‌آبادی، معاون وزیر خارجه ایران، هم اعلام کرد که هیئتی از قطر جمعه شب در تهران بوده و پس از «دوساعتی» گفت‌وگو به قطر بازگشته است. این در حالی است که دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در آخرین اظهار نظر خود گفته ایران تنها ظرف یک هفته گذشته بیشترین تعداد پهپاد تهاجمی و موشک را طی یک سال گذشته شلیک کرده است.

items.summary_original: Talk about talking turkey. Two feathered VIPs have checked into one of Washington's most luxurious hotels, complete with plush beds, a red-carpet welcome and a crowd of eager photographers, ahead of President Donald Trump's annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon at the White House. The presidential hopefuls arrived Sunday at the historic Willard InterContinental Washington, D.C., where they were photographed strutting across a red carpet, posing for pictures and standing atop the hotel's beds before their big day on the South Lawn. THE PENNSYLVANIA FARM BEHIND A WHITE HOUSE THANKSGIVING TURKEY TRADITION The U.S. Department of Agriculture celebrated their arrival on X, announcing a "SPECIAL DELIVERY TO WASHINGTON, D.C.!" and describing the birds as "two VERY special guests" receiving the presidential treatment. Photographs shared by the USDA, credited to the White House and National Turkey Federation, showed the plump white birds making their grand entrance before an audience of hotel guests and photographers. One turkey was even pictured riding through the hotel's ornate hallways inside a travel crate perched on a brass luggage cart. The pair appeared equally comfortable with the accommodations, with one bird spreading its feathers atop a neatly made bed while its companion stood nearby. items.summary_original: A Democratic New York City assemblyman addressed bizarre "lizard people" conspiracy theories after a viral video appeared to show his eyes rolling backward while standing behind Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a press conference. Jordan J.G. Wright was spotted during a press conference behind Mamdani on Friday, when the city announced plans to eventually shut down Rikers Island. As Mamdani spoke, Wright appeared to flash a slight grin before blinking and rolling his eyes in a circular motion toward the back of his head, prompting a wave of bizarre speculation online. "I have no idea what was going on in that video. I’m really not sure," Wright told the New York Post in a statement. NYC MAYOR MAMDANI ANNOUNCES DELAYED PLAN TO CLOSE CITY'S LARGEST JAIL He added that his work as an assemblyman speaks to his human character, pointing to a project he championed in Harlem that serves as the city's first community-based center dedicated to climate action. The five-story hub provides residents with environmental education and advocacy. "Obviously I’m a human being, and my humanity can be seen through my legislation like the $4 million for the WE ACT environmental justice center in Harlem," he said. "I can’t speak to any reptiles or aliens." The video sent social media users into a frenzy over the weekend, reigniting a decades-old conspiracy theory that extraterrestrial reptilians secretly control the Earth by disguising themselves as world leaders and celebrities to manipulate society. items.summary_original: A Russian warship capsized and sank Sunday after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck a naval base in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire, according to Libyan officials. Hours later, a second drone attack also hit a commercial ship off the coast of Benghazi, Reuters reported. The first ship, the Russian navy corvette Merkury, was docked at Benghazi Naval Base when two explosive-laden sea drones struck the vessel, according to Libyan military officials who spoke to The Associated Press . UKRAINE POUNDS BLACK SEA FLEET’S ‘LAST MAJOR STRONGHOLD’ WHILE PUTIN FLEXES NAVAL POWER IN PACIFIC At least four other drones were intercepted and destroyed, the officials said. Satellite images showed most of the warship capsized and submerged, with only its bow remaining above water. Smoke could be seen rising from the ship's superstructure, and debris was scattered along the pier. Ten people, including Russian and Libyan nationals, suffered minor injuries in the attack and were receiving treatment in Benghazi, medical sources told Reuters. The warship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply while returning to Russia under a maritime cooperation agreement with Libya's eastern-based government, officials said in a statement. Libyan military officials said an initial investigation indicated that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched from a base in western Libya , according to The AP. UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE

The reported operation would involve tankers sailing from Kharg Island, which handles most of Iran's crude oil exports, toward the Gulf of Oman and with crews reportedly assigned to the vessels and Iranian flags raised ahead of a possible attempt to breach the blockade. items.summary_original: Armenia is set to launch a U.S.-backed transportation and energy project along Iran's northern border Monday, despite warnings from a senior Iranian official that Tehran would "break their legs" if President Donald Trump and his allies crossed the Islamic Republic's "red line." Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan confirmed that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project would launch Monday, advancing the plan to connect mainland Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia and establish energy links with Turkey and Azerbaijan, Turkish media reported, citing Interfax. The project, a centerpiece of a U.S.-brokered peace initiative between Armenia and Azerbaijan, would also expand American economic involvement in the South Caucasus, where Iran has warned against any development it believes could threaten its security or regional influence. TRUMP'S FIRST IRAN WAR ESCALATION POST-MIDTERM LOSSES SEEKS TO CHOKE OFF TEHRAN’S TRADE The corridor has also gained strategic significance amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, as Tehran seeks to secure its northern trade routes and limit the U.S. security presence near its borders while Washington maintains its naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate focuses on Iran's borders. Speaking at the DigiTec 2026 technology conference in Yerevan, Pashinyan said the new TRIPP initiative, also known as the "Trump Corridor," would strengthen Armenia's regional energy connections, according to Interfax .

items.summary_original: Democrats have stormed back into power in the House, securing the largest majority of any party since 1992 in a sweeping midterm victory that will reshape the balance of power in Washington and leave Republicans with significantly less influence over the chamber. The victory was cemented after Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the House from North Carolina, according to The Associated Press (AP). He defeated longtime Republican incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx, who chaired the powerful House Rules Committee, which determines which bills reach the House floor for a vote. With several general election results still being called, Democrats have picked up 44 seats so far, giving them at least 258 seats in the House, their largest majority in more than three decades, according to The AP. STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE Meanwhile, Republicans have been left with at least 173 seats. Four House races remain undecided in Minnesota, Tennessee and two December runoffs in Louisiana, according to The AP. The party's projected majority will surpass its post-election totals in every election since Bill Clinton first won the presidency in 1992, when Democrats secured 258 seats, the outlet said. The party's next-largest showing reportedly came in 2008, when Barack Obama was elected president and Democrats won 257 House seats. The shift in the 435-member House will set the stage for a dramatic power struggle in Washington . WHAT THE

items.summary_original: President Donald Trump is warning that he is inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement, dismissing ongoing diplomatic talks with Tehran as meaningless. In exclusive comments Sunday to Fox News, the president accused Iranian negotiators of stalling while continuing to escalate hostilities following the U.S. elections. TRUMP KEEPS SIGNALING AN END TO IRAN WAR, BUT EXPERT WARNS A CRUCIAL PIECE OF HIS STRATEGY IS MISSING "They’re more aggressive now than before the election," Trump said, characterizing Iranian officials as "professional tap dancers." "They talk all the time, all they do is talk, but it’s all b------," he added. The remarks come as the U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports amid broader conflict in the Strait of Hormuz , and as Trump predicted that tit-for-tat strikes will continue between American and Iranian forces. PROTESTERS CALL FOR REGIME CHANGE IN IRAN FOLLOWING DEADLY CRASH THAT KILLED 13 OIL AND GAS WORKERS Trump also dared Tehran to challenge the U.S. naval siege. "I hope they do, they’ll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," Trump said regarding the possibility of Iranian forces testing the blockade. Meanwhile, anti-government demonstrations have flared up again in several Iranian cities. Asked about the renewed unrest inside the country, Trump offered a direct message to demonstrators on the ground: "Keep protesting."

items.summary_original: President Donald Trump predicted it would be "hard" to work with Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., if he is chosen to continue leading Senate Democrats next year. Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday that Schumer is likely to "fail again" if he is elected. Schumer is running for Senate majority leader once again, but opposition to his leadership is gaining steam. "It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader. He failed badly as 'Leader' once before, one of the worst in history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again," Trump wrote. DEMOCRATS TURN ON SCHUMER AFTER HISTORIC ELECTION WINS AS POTENTIAL CHALLENGER EMERGES "All he did was perpetuate the Russia, Russia, Russia Hoax, and many other Hoaxes and Scams, making my victory in 2024 an easy and glorious one. items.summary_original: House Democrats are pushing to raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, calling the current hourly pay a "remnant of slavery" to "oppress women," despite warnings from conservative economists that the proposal could drive up costs and threaten jobs. The proposal from the Congressional Progressive Caucus would more than triple the current $7.25 federal minimum wage, raising questions about its potential impact on businesses and workers in states with significantly lower living costs than major cities. "We should be rallying around (a minimum wage of) $25 at minimum, and it should be cost adjusted for inflation , so that people can have a job that enables them to survive and thrive," Rep. Everton Blair Jr., D-Ga., told Fox News Digital. AOC-BACKED $25 MINIMUM WAGE PLAN SOUNDS GREAT — BUT AT WHAT COST? Asked whether a nationwide $25 minimum wage could hurt workers and businesses in lower-cost states, Blair argued that the proposed rate should serve as a national baseline. The congressman said $25 an hour should be "the floor" and "should be higher in places with a higher cost of living." Blair acknowledged concerns that raising the minimum wage could contribute to inflation but said lawmakers must find a way to increase workers' earnings while "keeping people afloat." Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., echoed Blair's support for the proposal, pointing to the high cost of living in cities such as Seattle and Washington, D.C., as justification for raising wages. Bolsonaro said that he fled for the sake of Brazil, to continue the fight against Alexandre de Moraes and the Brazilian Supreme Court, and alleging both election interference and political persecution. The operation began around 8:05 a.m. PT as travelers boarded an Alaska Airlines flight, according to the Department of Homeland Security. DHS says ICE officers targeted Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, whom the agency described as a Mexican national "who overstayed his visa." During the arrest, other travelers began getting in the officers' way, and one passenger threw hot coffee at the agents, DHS said. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, told Fox News Digital. items.summary_original: A massive fire tore through a three-story candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province, killing at least three workers and likely more, and leaving dozens of others unaccounted for as emergency crews fought persistent hotspots into Sunday. Indonesian police removed 24 body bags amid battling the smoldering fire and pausing a search for missing workers overnight, which will resume Monday morning. There were reportedly as many as 300 present for their Saturday shift, but the factory said 24 of the 65 workers involved had returned home, four were receiving medical treatment, 29 remained missing and the whereabouts of another eight had yet to be confirmed. Body bags might contain remains from several people because the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable, police said. The fire broke out at 5 p.m. local time Saturday at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia facility in the Cikande area of the Serang district, which borders the capital, Jakarta. Authorities are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers. The identification process could take two to three weeks, Hidayati added. items.summary_original: A lawsuit challenging Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to commute 548 death sentences is raising questions about the governor's clemency powers, with a legal expert arguing Newsom is using his gubernatorial authority to circumvent the will of voters who have repeatedly rejected efforts to abolish capital punishment. Newsom announced Nov. 5 that he intends to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the Golden State's death row to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, a move that will take effect only after the necessary legal steps are completed. The Criminal Justice Legal Foundation (CJLF) on Sunday filed a lawsuit at the California Supreme Court seeking to block Newsom's proposed sweeping commutation, citing the governor's "failure to provide legally required notice to district attorneys and his disregard for the rights of victims and their families to be notified and heard," according to a news release. Newsom may be using clemency to impose his own views on capital punishment despite voters repeatedly rejecting abolition, Zack Smith, a senior legal fellow for Courts and the Constitution at the Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday. The investors allege that Spanish construction giant ACS and companies to tied its former subsidiary Cobra, misled federal officials into approving the grant by claiming the troubled solar plant was ready for use, even though it had suffered major construction problems and was shut down for months following a molten-salt-tank failure. items.summary_original: A Jewish American activist in New York City decried what he calls "anti-Jewish discrimination" after the student government at a school that is part of the City University of New York (CUNY) system, canceled an event that was supposed to include the school's Hillel group when it received backlash from other student organizations. Hunter College's undergraduate student government (USG) canceled a "Cultural Arts Night" involving several student groups, including Hunter Hillel, the Chinese Student Scholar Association, the Taiwanese Student Association and the Center for Puerto Rican Studies, according to the New York Post . The radical far-left group Students for Justice in Palestine reportedly took part in planning the event. In a statement to The Post, the school itself admitted that some of those groups withdrew from the event because Hunter Hillel was planning to participate. items.summary_original: Hakeem Jeffries once called his deep ties to Jerusalem an extension of his representation of New York City as he touted his support for Israel and the Jewish community. But those comments from 2020, recently resurfaced and going viral, may come back to bite the Democratic House leader as the progressive wing of the party — and even some establishment members — continue to further break with the U.S. maintaining support for the Jewish state. "Someone said to me, ‘Hakeem, you’re going to Israel a 5th time?’" Jeffries recalled in an interview with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) more than six years ago. "I said, ‘listen, I’m from New York City' — and back home in New York City, we consider Jerusalem to be the 6th Borough. And so, I’m just trying to catch up with my constituents." The comments resurfaced just after he won his party's nomination to be speaker of the House in the next Congress. JEFFRIES SURVIVES DEM VOTE TO SECURE SPEAKER POSITION AS PROGRESSIVE RESISTANCE CLOUDS HIS CHANCES The remarks from 2020 contrast starkly with a growing faction of the Democratic Party that has condemned AIPAC and the political favor Israel has historically enjoyed among lawmakers. The clip also raises questions over how far Jeffries will go to placate calls for a more critical review of U.S.-Israel relations in light of his previous support for the Jewish state. items.summary_original: A powerful apex predator has reignited a fierce battle between farmers demanding greater control over gray wolves killing their livestock and environmentalists fighting to keep them shielded — a decision the Trump administration must now weigh that could shape the future of wildlife management. One longtime Minnesota farmer has spent years grappling with the loss of several of his calves killed by gray wolves, also known as timber wolves, roaming around his property in the middle of the night. "We can walk right outside of our door and hear the howling of these timber wolves, and it'll send shivers down your spine because you have seen what they can do, and they're the top-of-the-line predator," Shayne Isane told Fox News Digital. "There's nothing that hunts them. No other animals they are afraid of." ARCTIC WOLF ATTACKS CHILD DURING ZOOKEEPER EVENT, GIRL AIRLIFTED TO HOSPITAL Isane, who has farmed for nearly four decades, said he is one of many farmers struggling to defend his livestock from gray wolves . Despite losing thousands of dollars and fearing for the safety of his nearly 300 cattle, Isane said he is unable to handle the threat himself. "Even if we see them attacking our livestock, we can't shoot or try to help out our animals," he said. "It's just against the law. We can't do it, only in the case of the threat of human life, which is a tough sell for us, because when you see them very close to your livelihood, your families and your livestock, it's a huge concern."

items.summary_original: A sweeping federal watchdog report found that 17 of 22 major civilian agencies failed to fully address key cybersecurity planning guidance, warning that the shortcomings could leave government systems more vulnerable to cyberattacks and operational disruptions. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) released its findings this week, identifying gaps at the Departments of Homeland Security (DHS), Justice ( DOJ ), State , Treasury and Health and Human Services (HHS), among others. The report examined whether agencies had incorporated selected federal guidance into their plans for implementing zero trust architecture, a cybersecurity approach requiring users, devices and systems to be verified before accessing protected networks. RETIRED FBI AGENT WARNS NCIC BREACH COULD THREATEN POLICE SAFETY DURING TRAFFIC STOPS Only five of the 22 agencies fully addressed the selected guidance as of August 2026, prompting GAO to issue 40 recommendations to the remaining 17. "Agencies would therefore be at increased risk of cyberattacks that could interrupt operations or otherwise compromise agency resources," GAO warned. HHS received six recommendations, the most of any agency reviewed, after investigators found that it lacked a documented enterprise-wide zero trust implementation plan covering all its information systems. items.summary: یک مامور ویژه نظارتی بازنشسته FBI روز شنبه هشدار داد که اگر هکرها سوابق داخل پایگاه داده را تغییر دهند، یک نفوذ سایبری به مرکز اطلاعات جرایم ملی (NCIC) این اداره می تواند افسران پلیس را در هنگام توقف ترافیک به خطر بیندازد. جیسون پک، یک مامور ویژه نظارتی سابق FBI که در جرایم سایبری و اطلاعات عمومی کار می کرد، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت که تیم واکنش به حوادث این اداره باید به سرعت تعیین کند که آیا داده ها در داخل سیستم دستکاری شده اند یا خیر. پک با اشاره به اینکه هنوز هیچ نشانه ای مبنی بر تغییر سوابق یا قطعی بودن سیستم وجود ندارد، گفت: "آنچه آنها نگران آن هستند این است که اگر هر یک از این داده ها تغییر کرده باشد، ممکن است ایمنی افسران در کنار جاده را تحت تاثیر قرار دهد." items.summary_original: A retired FBI supervisory special agent warned Saturday that a cyber intrusion into the bureau's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) could endanger police officers during traffic stops if hackers altered records inside the database. Jason Pack, a former FBI supervisory special agent who worked in cybercrime and public information, told Fox News Digital that the bureau's incident response team must quickly determine whether data was manipulated inside the system, which feeds criminal records to patrol cars nationwide. "What they worry about is if any of this data has changed, then it might affect officers' safety on the side of the road," Pack said, noting there is no indication yet that any records were altered or that the system is experiencing an outage. FBI PROBES SECOND CYBERATTACK IN MONTHS AS HACKERS BREACH KEY CRIME DATABASE, SOURCES SAY Three sources familiar with the matter told Fox News that hackers breached the NCIC, marking the second cyberattack against the bureau in months. The FBI is investigating how the intruders gained entry and whether any information was compromised. In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the intrusion, adding, "I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that." items.summary_original: Former Kansas Republican Sen. Sam Brownback, who served as an ambassador during Donald Trump's first term, blamed the president's personal leadership style for Republicans' midterm losses. He claims the outcome of the 2026 elections — where Democrats' sweeping victories in traditional red strongholds helped them reclaim majorities in the House and Senate — was a sign of voters rejecting Trump more than rebuking his policies. "I think the thing we're missing is that it was really targeted at President Trump. I don't think it was targeted at the policies so much," Brownback told Fox News Digital in an interview. "Pride comes before a fall and a haughty spirit before a stumble." REPUBLICANS TURN ON TRUMP AFTER DEVASTATING MIDTERM LOSSES HAND DEMOCRATS CONTROL OF CONGRESS The former Kansas governor argued that Republicans should not write off the midterm results as the typical losses suffered by a president’s party through history during their second term. Brownback, who represented Kansas in the U.S. Senate from 1996 to 2011 before serving as governor from 2011 to 2018, said economic concerns, including inflation and gas prices , played a role in the election results. He suggested voters' frustrations extended beyond the economy to Trump's approach to governing. John Cornyn is doing a "tremendous disservice" by blocking his pick to fill a judicial seat in Dallas. "We're going to have a radical left lunatic get in there, and we don't want that," the president said. Trump's comments come after Cornyn told The Associated Press he has no intention of returning the "blue slip" for T. Elliot Gaiser, a Department of Justice senior lawyer who was nominated by the president to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas. TRUMP TAKES AIM AT SENATE 'BLUE SLIP' TRADITION AS GOP RESISTS CHANGE The blue slip tradition allows for home state senators to weigh in on judicial nominees, giving them a say on who does and doesn’t move forward. Returning a blue slip is the equivalent of giving a thumbs up to the nominees moving forward, while keeping the slip effectively blocks the process. "Everybody tells me he's outstanding, and he's being held up by John Cornyn because John Cornyn's feelings were hurt," said Trump, who endorsed Cornyn's challenger, Ken Paxton, in the Texas Republican Senate primary. items.summary_original: Hackers breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC), three sources familiar with the matter told Fox News, marking the second cyberattack against the bureau in months. The FBI is investigating the hack to determine the unauthorized entry point, but, for now, it is unclear what information was compromised, sources said. The NCIC database is a critical information-sharing tool for federal, state and local authorities, helping them track fugitives, monitor registered sex offenders, check whether someone has failed a gun background check, among other information. In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. TECH OUTAGE CASCADE EXPOSES US VULNERABILITIES TO FOREIGN CYBER THREATS "I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that," Trump added. The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. CNN first reported the hack. In September, a group called ShinyHunters hacked into the FBI's job portal website intending to steal sensitive employment records. The mysterious group, known for extortion plots, claimed it stole sensitive information belonging to almost every FBI agent, including names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, assignments and, in some cases, the names of family members. items.summary_original: A Biden-appointed judge in California issued a preliminary injunction barring Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins from using her official email or authority to send unwelcome religious messages to employees, finding two of Rollins' previous holiday messages promoting Christianity "go too far" and amounted to "coercive" pressure on nonbelieving employees. Thursday's ruling from U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson comes as President Donald Trump's administration has sought in his second term to expand religious expression protections for federal workers, including through 2025 Office of Personnel Management guidance allowing employees to display religious items and to discuss their faith at work and the creation of a White House Faith Office . However, Thompson found that two emails Rollins sent to all U.S. Department of Agriculture employees that referred to Jesus Christ as "our Savior" and "our risen Lord" during the 2025 Christmas and 2026 Easter seasons likely violated the First Amendment's establishment clause. FEDERAL EMPLOYEES ACCUSE USDA SECRETARY OF 'CHRISTIAN PROSELYTIZING' IN HOLIDAY EMAILS TO STAFF "The wisdom of the Founders was in recognizing that independence requires freedom of conscience," Thompson ruled. "The command of the Establishment Clause, thus, is to prohibit the government from using its authority to try to sway an individual's decision about whether and how to practice their faith." items.summary_original: TONOPAH, Nev. — An Obama-era solar power plant once hailed as a "clean energy marvel" and backed by more than $1 billion in federal support has gone bankrupt for a second time and sold for just $7 million with the estimated taxpayer tab potentially reaching $507.6 million. Rising from the barren Nevada desert, the Crescent Dunes Solar Energy Project looks like a futuristic fortress in a vast, dusty wasteland, with more than 10,000 mirrors surrounding a giant central tower. The plant was designed to generate solar electricity even after sunset, using an emerging technology that promised to revolutionize green energy in America . The Obama administration bet big on the project, backing it with a $737 million federal loan guarantee and around $275 million in Treasury grant awards as part of its broader $90 billion push to combat climate change and stimulate the economy after the 2008 financial crisis. OBAMA-ERA 'CLEAN ENERGY' SOLAR POWER PLANT STILL USES FOSSIL FUELS – AND KILLS THOUSANDS OF BIRDS ANNUALLY But the promise never matched the performance. After operations began in late 2015, leaks and equipment failures repeatedly knocked the plant offline, production fell short and cheaper solar alternatives undercut its economics, driving the project into financial ruin and leaving taxpayers shouldering the cost. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump signed an executive order late Friday instructing federal contractors to notify the White House of congressional information requests and to withhold material the administration deems privileged, a move that comes as Democrats prepare to launch oversight investigations. The order applies to all federal contractors and subcontractors. Companies that fail to comply risk losing their existing contracts or being suspended from future work, according to the order. Trump framed the directive as pushback against lawmakers whom the order accuses of "harassing private companies" to get confidential executive branch information. SUPREME COURT URGED TO DEFANG ‘CRIMINAL TRAP’ THAT HAS SENT TRUMP OFFICIALS TO PRISON The order could invite legal challenges, particularly if contractors are told to withhold records sought by subpoena. Although executive privilege lets presidents protect certain internal communications, courts can intervene in clashes over congressional oversight powers. The order builds on a directive issued earlier this week by White House Counsel Will Scharf , who instructed federal agencies to clear employee congressional testimony with the administration first. Scharf added that some Democratic investigations could cross into criminal conduct, drawing pushback over what critics call a broader effort to shield the executive branch from oversight. items.summary_original: Incoming Senate Republican campaign Chairman Bernie Moreno says the party faces a "very tough" road ahead as the GOP aims to take back its majority in 2028 after taking significant losses in the midterms earlier this month. Democrats convincingly grabbed control of the Senate and will hold a 56-44 majority when the new Congress is sworn in at the start of the new year. They also won control of the House, and multiple governors' seats flipped from red to blue. In the Senate, the new split means Republicans will need to flip at least six seats in the 2028 elections to win back the majority. That number rises to seven seats if they lose the White House in the next election cycle. SENATE REPUBLICANS FEAR 'BRUTAL' 2028 MAP COULD KEEP DEMOCRATS IN POWER FOR YEARS One senator told Fox News Digital Republicans can "forget 2028." "It is an absolutely brutal map," Moreno recently told Fox News Digital, pointing to the states up for grabs in 2028. But the first-term senator from Ohio added that, in "politics, things change pretty quickly." He's not kidding. At the start of the 2026 cycle , the Democrats faced a steep and narrow path to winning back the majority, but, by Election Day, the party was able to ride a massive blue wave formed by a favorable political climate to flip nine Senate seats. Now, experts tell Fox News Digital that the group from a bygone era was right as the safety net program hurtles toward a crisis that could affect millions. "Social Security benefits were put on autopilot back in 1977," Andrew Biggs, a senior fellow of the American Enterprise Institute, told Fox News Digital. "Since then, Congress has done as little as it possibly could." Senate Budget Committee Chair Ron Johnson, R-Wis., unveiled a report on the decades-old program that blasted it as a "Ponzi scheme" and warned that Social Security’s slide into insolvency began in the 1970s, when, despite warnings, lawmakers opted to tie benefit growth to wages rather than inflation. Still, lawmakers at the time ran with their own amendments to the program, which were signed into law by former President Jimmy Carter in December 1977. items.summary: براندون جانسون، شهردار دموکرات شیکاگو در حالی مبارزه می کند که نام خود را در برگه رای 2027 حفظ کند، زیرا دولت او در یک فروپاشی مالی و رهبری در تالار شهر غرق شده است. مقامات انتخاباتی در حال بررسی چالش‌ها برای بیش از 25000 امضای نامزدی جانسون در آستانه انتخابات شهرداری 23 فوریه 2027 هستند، جنگی که تنها چند روز پس از استعفای ناگهانی سومین مدیر مالی وی در 10 ماه گذشته آغاز شد، استاندارد پورز سه سال رای منفی به شورای شهر داد و 5 سال اعتباری را در شورای شهر بررسی کرد. گزارشگری مالی شهر برای تحریف های احتمالی علیرغم فشارهای فزاینده، جانسون سؤالات مربوط به اینکه آیا از چالش رای‌گیری جان سالم به در می‌برد یا نه، پاسخ داد. جانسون به ABC 7 گفت: "آره، احساس خوبی دارم. من در رای گیری شرکت خواهم کرد."
items.summary_original: Democratic Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson is fighting to keep his name on the 2027 ballot with his administration is engulfed in a fiscal and leadership meltdown at City Hall. Election officials are reviewing challenges to more than 25,000 of Johnson's nominating signatures ahead of the Feb. 23, 2027, mayoral election, a threshold fight unfolding just days after his third chief financial officer in 10 months abruptly resigned, Standard Poor's placed Chicago's credit rating on negative watch and the City Council voted 45-5 to investigate three years of city financial reporting for possible misstatements. Despite the mounting pressure, Johnson brushed off questions about whether he will survive the ballot challenge. "Yeah, feeling just fine. I'm going to be on the ballot," Johnson told ABC 7 Chicago about the challenge. "Looking forward to building the safest, most affordable big city in America, and we're going to continue to do that work." CHICAGO'S 12-LANGUAGE BALLOTS MAKE ELECTIONS 'HARDER TO MONITOR,' ILLINOIS GOP CHAIR WARNS Johnson needs 12,500 valid signatures to qualify for Chicago's Feb. 23, 2027, mayoral ballot. Hearing officers at the Chicago Board of Elections are reviewing more than 25,000 signatures challenged by supporters of perennial mayoral candidate Willie Wilson. items.summary_original: Ukraine 's repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge, one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most prized infrastructure projects, have dealt a potentially significant blow to Moscow's military supply routes into occupied Crimea, raising questions about Russia's ability to sustain operations as both sides prepare for a difficult winter. A European intelligence assessment dated Nov. 18 and obtained by Fox News Digital describes Ukraine's latest assault as likely its most successful attack on the heavily defended crossing, following a coordinated campaign targeting Russian air defenses, radar and electronic warfare systems. Ret. Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, told Fox News Digital the consequences could extend far beyond the destruction of a symbolic Russian landmark. "The Russians are extremely limited in how they get supplies to Crimea and cutting the Kerch bridge will severely, severely damage their ability to resupply Crimea," Breedlove said. UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY' On Nov. 17, Ukrainian missiles and drones struck the 12-mile bridge linking Russia's Krasnodar region to Crimea, collapsing a major section of the roadway into the Kerch Strait and damaging the adjacent railway. items.summary_original: The Republican chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee has warned of an ongoing ‘horrific trend’ of Christians being killed in Africa . Earlier this month, at least 34 people, the majority said to be Ethiopian Orthodox Christians, were killed in a village in the Arsi Zone, about 250 miles southeast of Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa. "The attacks on Christians in Ethiopia are a horrific trend," Sen. Jim Risch, R-Idaho, told Fox News Digital in a statement, adding, "The instability and violence in Ethiopia has grave consequences for Ethiopian civilians, the region and American interests." NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES Open Doors UK Ireland told Fox News Digital there has been a string of killings in the area, with some 60 Orthodox Christians killed just two weeks before this attack in November. Open Doors is an international organization supporting persecuted Christians. A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital they are aware of "reports of killing in Arsi Zone," adding: "Reports of civilian killings in Ethiopia demand action. We call for independent investigations and accountability." The Addis Standard online news outlet reported gunmen approached St. Mary’s Church in Endeto, Robe District, and at the main entrance shouted "Surrender" before opening fire. items.summary: قزاقستان در سال‌های اخیر تلاش گسترده‌ای را برای بازتعریف روایت تاریخی خود آغاز کرده و به‌طور فزاینده بر پیوندش با اردوی زرین تاکید می‌کند. مقام‌های این کشور می‌گویند قزاقستان اکنون حق خود را برای روایت مستقل تاریخش به کار گرفته است، اما این رویکرد تازه در عین حال با برداشت رایج در روسیه از گذشته قزاق‌ها در تضاد قرار دارد. منتقدان آن را بخشی از پروژه هویت‌سازی ملی و سیاست خارجی قاسم‌جومارت توقایف می‌دانند؛ پروژه‌ای که قزاقستان را نه فقط وارث خانات قزاق، بلکه جانشین مستقیم اردوی زرین معرفی می‌کند.

items.summary_original: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling on the U.S. to quickly organize talks with Russia with the full participation of European negotiators and advisors in what would mark a first-of-its-kind meeting. He made the call Thursday after meeting with several U.S. and European leaders in Berlin at the Coalition of the Willing summit, which focused on security guarantees aimed at deterring future Russian aggression. During the meeting, U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner announced that Moscow and President Donald Trump had agreed to a multilateral negotiating format involving Europe. "We are counting on the American side to help organize the first multilateral meeting at the team level, with full European participation, as soon as possible," Zelenskyy said. The push signals an effort to prevent Europe and Kyiv from being sidelined in U.S.-Russia talks . KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE "From the very beginning, Ukraine has advocated for this approach — maximum coordination among us on everything concerning European and Ukrainian security and our future," Zelenskyy said. "We need to work quickly, and this is the only approach Ukraine is taking. The more actively the discussions move forward, the greater the chances of achieving real progress." items.summary_original: Two Iranian twin sisters imprisoned for participating in anti-government protests came face-to-face with the very official they accused of torturing and sexually assaulting them when they appeared in court to seek justice. They discovered he was the judge assigned to hear their complaint, their U.S.-based cousin told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. Masoud Nourmohammadi, the cousin of Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, alleged that the official had been involved in their interrogation and subsequently presided over the complaint they filed against the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). "As soon as they walk in, they see the exact person who tortured them and sexually assaulted them is the judge," Nourmohammadi said. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS; THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN He claimed the complaint was immediately dismissed by that same official. "The judge was their prosecutor during the building (of) the case, and he was the one that did the sexual assault on the kids and tortured them as a prosecutor and for the lawsuit he was assigned as a judge for that lawsuit," Nourmohammadi said. Fox News Digital has not independently verified the allegations or reviewed the court documents. The twins, now 21, were arrested after January anti-government demonstrations in Isfahan . items.summary_original: A "terrorist attack" by the Iran-backed Houthis damaged multiple floors at the tallest skyscraper in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund on Thursday, authorities and reports said. Entrances leading into the King Abdullah Financial District were closed and people were being evacuated from the area following the strike by a suspected Houthi missile, according to Reuters. The news agency reported that the attack on the Public Investment Fund Tower, which is 80 stories tall, destroyed windows across up to eight floors of the building and bent portions of its metal facade. "One of the towers of the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, causing material damage but no injuries — praise be to God," the General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense wrote on X as it shared a photo of the damage. HOUTHIS KILL 14 AT SAUDI AIRPORT AS EXPERT WARNS OF 'RAPID TARGETS' AMID MIDDLE EAST WAR The incident unfolded after the Houthis attacked a building belonging to Saudi state-owned oil company Aramco, in the same area on Nov. 8, Reuters reported. Saudi-led coalition spokesman Col. Turki Al-Malki said Thursday that Saudi air defenses "intercepted and destroyed 4 ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward the southern region." items.summary_original: President Donald Trump issued a joint "peace declaration" with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday following the trio's trilateral meeting during the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China. "The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security," the White House said in a statement, titled "U.S.-Russia-China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace." Russia's Foreign Ministry and China's Chamber of Commerce to the EU confirmed the pact in near-identical statements, which also highlighted the three countries' commitment to reducing nuclear proliferation, increasing global petroleum production and upholding international institutions. TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE "The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows," each of the U.S., Chinese and Russian statements read. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs also released a more expansive statement on the meeting. The officials raised concerns that Beijing is seeking to acquire sophisticated U.S. semiconductors and access powerful AI data centers, potentially strengthening its military capabilities without the knowledge or involvement of the American companies behind the technology. Those concerns are underscored by the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission's 2026 annual report , which says Beijing is seeking to circumvent American export controls to obtain advanced semiconductors for military modernization. BEYOND KILLER ROBOTS: CHINA'S REAL AI THREAT TO AMERICA IS ALREADY HERE, EXPERTS WARN Citing an April 2026 assessment by Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, the commission reported that China's People's Liberation Army was soliciting advanced Nvidia chips for AI-enabled military capabilities. The report describes Beijing's push toward "intelligentized warfare," integrating AI into weapons systems, targeting, military command and logistics. Mike Kuiken, the commission's vice chairman, warned that the threat extends beyond chip exports to access to computing infrastructure abroad. items.summary: ولادیمیر پوتین، رئیس‌جمهور روسیه روز پنجشنبه متعهد شد که پس از آسیب شدید نیروهای ولدیمیر زلنسکی به پل تنگه کرچ که به نماد الحاق کریمه به روسیه تبدیل شده است، به اوکراین به شیوه‌ای «دردناک‌تر» پاسخ دهد. این هشدار زمانی صادر شد که رئیس جمهور اوکراین گفت که برای گفتگو با بیش از 40 شریک با هدف پایان دادن به جنگ، از جمله با داماد و مشاور رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ، جرد کوشنر و فرستاده ویژه ایالات متحده، استیو ویتکاف، وارد برلین آلمان شده است. پوتین پس از دیدار با رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ و رئیس جمهور چین شی جین پینگ برای گفتگوهای سه جانبه در حاشیه آسیا و اقیانوسیه گفت: "ما به این حملات پاسخ خواهیم داد. و من می خواهم همه این را بدانند: من معتقدم پاسخ ما بسیار دردناک تر از آنچه رژیم کیف بر روی پل انجام داد خواهد بود."
items.summary_original: Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed Thursday to respond to Ukraine in a "far more painful" manner after Volodymyr Zelenskyy's forces heavily damaged the Kerch Strait bridge that has become a symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea. The warning was issued as Ukraine's president said he arrived in Berlin, Germany for talks with more than 40 partners aimed at ending the war, including with President Donald Trump's son-in-law and advisor Jared Kushner and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff. "We will respond to these strikes. And I want everyone to know this: I believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge," Putin said after meeting with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping for trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, according to Reuters. "We will, of course, restore the bridge. The road section suffered serious damage," Putin reportedly added. UKRAINE RELEASE VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE PUTIN'S PRIZE BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA Ukraine attacked the bridge for the third time this week prior to Putin making his remarks, Reuters reported. A Russian official told The Associated Press that the latest strike on the bridge linking Russia to Crimea halted rail traffic. items.summary_original: The leaders of Syria ’s oldest Christian denominations issued a dire warning about the intensified persecution of their communities and whether there is a future for them in the Middle Eastern nation. Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, a former U.S.-designated terrorist who commanded the al Qaeda-linked Nusra Front during the nation's civil war, has since sought to distance himself from his extremist past as he oversees the nation's rebuilding amid a deteriorating situation for Christians and other minorities. Senior Christians released a joint statement that noted "a series of heinous and recurring attacks targeting the Syrian people, and Christians in particular. Time and again, we have raised our voices, and we continue to do so, as this wave of attacks has persisted without interruption. These attacks are not, and have never been, isolated incidents." The signers were John X, Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East, Ignatius Aphrem II, Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East, and Youssef Absi, Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarch of Antioch and All the East. Farmers say the attacks have resulted in significant livestock losses and warn that poisoned food and water sources could also endanger other animals and nearby residents. The trend gained attention following an investigation by The Press Service of Israel (TPS-IL) that identified a cluster of poisoning incidents at farms across the Binyamin region over the past 12 months. CHRISTIAN ZIONISTS TAKE ON ANTI-ISRAEL ‘PROPAGANDA’ FROM BIBLICAL HEARTLAND In a TPS-IL video, an Israeli farmer alleged that poisonings took place with substances placed within food such as dates and pita bread. "We have two populations with warm blood," the source said, referring to Israelis and Palestinians in the contested region. "Sometimes this manifests as verbal or physical violence, attacks, arson, property damage and, among other things, agricultural terrorism involving harm to animals." items.summary_original: Thousands of people in Haiti took to the streets Tuesday in a show of support for Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele deploying troops to the country to combat violent armed gangs. The demonstration unfolded as Haiti's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Patrick Pélissier, prepared to travel to San Salvador to discuss anti-gang strategies and ongoing troop cooperation. The president reflected on the moment in a post on X, sharing a video capturing a sea of people chanting, dancing and cheering in celebration. "I never expected anything like this. I hear you loud and clear. I love you too. We will triumph. God will give us victory," Bukele said. BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR According to Reuters, some demonstrators carried signs reading "Long live Bukele" and "Down with the gangs," while others voiced their support for the Salvadoran leader. "Only a week of operation, we can see the path to change in Haiti. We say thank you to Bukele for all the help he gives us," demonstrator Claudy Mayas said. Another demonstrator said Bukele was providing Haitians with the one thing they had been waiting years for. "Four years ago, I could not go to Champs de Mars. I couldn't go to the south of Haiti," a demonstrator, also identified as Claude, said. "We don’t ask much of the government. We don’t ask for jobs. We need only security." items.summary_original: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned Wednesday that Bahrain's monarchy faces an existential threat as Iranian drones and missiles targeted U.S. military installations in the Gulf kingdom. Tehran's warning came amid renewed attacks on Bahrain, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, and a regional expert warned of Iran's decades-long efforts to destabilize the island nation and assert territorial claims. "This is a regime that has tried to inflame tensions there for quite literally several decades and has claims to the island nation as well," Behnam Ben Taleblu , a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital. BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES "The Islamic Republic is also trying to use military force to evict the United States from the region," he added. In a warning directed at Bahrain's ruling Al Khalifa family, IRGC Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi accused the monarchy of cooperating with military action against Iran , relying on U.S. protection and challenging Shiite religious authority. "Colluding in the aggression against Islamic Iran, living inside the American security bubble, and encroaching on the authority of the Shiite religious leadership are three fundamental mistakes being made by the Al Khalifa regime," Mohebbi wrote on X . items.summary_original: People practicing the Islamic faith are poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, becoming the world's largest religion, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Center. The detailed report attributes the shift primarily to higher fertility rates and younger populations among Muslims, who are growing at a faster rate than other major faiths. "Around the world, we find that Muslims tend to have more children than non-Muslims, [and] they tend to be younger as a result of having more children in the past," Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett told Fox News Digital. WHY PEOPLE REALLY STOPPED HAVING KIDS: NEW STUDY UNCOVERS THE SURPRISING REASONS FAMILIES ARE SHRINKING Muslims have the highest fertility rate at 3.1 children per woman, followed by Christians at 2.5, according to the study. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women gave birth to 252 million babies, more than women of any other religion and compared to 208 million born to Christian mothers. If trends continue, the United States will also undergo a major religious shift . While Christians currently account for roughly 62% to 64% of U. Other images show tools allegedly used in the attack and O'Corrain standing on the aircraft's roof before his arrest.
